newsitem.title: JORDAN: U.S. envoy tells King Hussein of peace progress.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy tells King Hussein of peace progress.

text.p: U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross told Jordan's King Hussein on Saturday that Israel and the Palestinians had narrowed differences over a long delayed Israeli troop redeployment from the West Bank town of Hebron, the state news agency Petra said.

It said Ross, who is shuttling between Israel and Palestinian self-rule areas, conveyed the remarks in a telephone conversation with King Hussein to brief him on progress in Israeli-Palestinian talks to push ahead faltering Middle East peace accords.
"Mr Ross confirmed to His Majesty King Hussein that the gap between the two sides had narrowed," Petra said.

Israeli and Palestinian negotiators have been trying to clinch a Hebron deal in nearly three weeks of U.S.-brokered talks. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said this week an agreement was close but accused Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat of procrastinating.
Ross also told King Hussein of a meeting to be held later in the day between the Israeli and Palestinian negotiating teams at the Tel Aviv home of the U.S. ambassador in Israel.

"The meeting will try to overcome obstacles and try to reach an accord over redeployment in Hebron to allow negotiators to move ahead to implement other accords related to the interim accord," Ross was quoted as telling the king.

King Hussein, regarded as Israel's strongest Arab ally since Jordan signed a peace treaty with the Jewish state in 1994, has recently warned of renewed violence in the region if Israel does not honour its peace accords with the Palestinians.
